checks.prompt: Stations `P` and `Q` sit at `-9 m` and `-3 m` on a pipe run. Find `PQ`.

responses.why: consistent with reading `-9 - (-3)` as `-9 - 3`, which mishandles the double sign.

followUp.solution: `|-3 - 4| = |-7| = 7` metres. Reading `-3 - 4` as `-1` would give a one-metre weld gap instead of seven.

checks.prompt: Three marks give `DE = 8`, `EF = 5`, `DF = 11`. Is `E` between `D` and `F`?

options.label: No, and the three are not collinear at all
No, but they are still on one line
options.why: consistent with stopping at the failed addition. If the three were on one line in any order, one of the three additions would have worked; none does.

options.label: Yes
options.why: consistent with applying the addition rule without testing it. `8 + 5 = 13`, which is not `11`.

checks.solution: `8 + 5 = 13 ≠ 11`, so `E` is not between them. And since the two shorter lengths exceed the longest, the marks form a triangle.

followUp.prompt: Marks `A`, `B`, `C` lie in that order with `AC = 30` and `AB = 11`. Find `BC`.
followUp.solution: `BC = AC - AB = 30 - 11 = 19`, the same postulate rearranged.

checks.prompt: `P`, `Q`, `R` lie in that order with `PQ = 2x + 1`, `QR = x - 3`, `PR = 25`. Find `x`.

responses.why: consistent with solving for `PQ` rather than for `x`. `PQ = 2(9) + 1 = 19`.
consistent with dropping the `-2` when collecting terms, solving `3x = 25` and rounding.
